title: Comunicado 2025-07-31
summary: The SARB MPC unanimously cut the repo rate 25bp to 7.00%, citing a stronger rand, moderating inflation expectations, headline at 3% and core at 2.9%, and a weaker 2025 growth outlook, with balanced risks to both growth and inflation and no explicit guidance on the next move. The big change versus the May statement is that the 3% inflation objective moves from an illustrative scenario to the Committee's stated preference: the MPC will now aim for the bottom of the 3-6% range and use forecasts with a 3% anchor at future meetings. That framework shift cuts both ways: under the old 4.5% anchor the model had rates bottoming around 7% (i.e. roughly at today's level), while the 3% path implies about five more cuts over the medium term, albeit with temporarily higher real rates and a modest growth sacrifice. The vote also moved from 5-1, with one member preferring a 50bp cut in May, to unanimous, removing the dovish dissent. Net, a cut that keeps modest further easing on the table through the new 3% anchor, framed around locking in low inflation rather than urgency.

key_quotes.quote: Against this backdrop, the MPC decided to reduce the policy rate by 25 basis points, to 7%, with effect from the 1st of August. The decision was unanimous.
key_quotes.context: 25bp cut to 7%, unanimous (May was 5-1 with one member for 50bp)

key_quotes.quote: Therefore, the MPC now prefers inflation to settle at 3%. In line with this, we have decided to aim for the bottom of our inflation target range, of 3-6%.
key_quotes.context: The 3% objective moves from scenario (May) to the Committee's preference

key_quotes.quote: By contrast, the forecast for a 3% objective has roughly five more cuts, over the medium term, taking interest rates slightly below 6%.
key_quotes.context: Under the 4.5% anchor rates bottom around 7%; the 3% anchor, now used for forecasts, implies further easing

key_quotes.quote: The risks to this outlook appear balanced.
key_quotes.context: Balanced inflation risks despite an expected near-term rise in headline from food and fuel
